boundary_rationale: Opens with the formulaic וַיְהִי בִּימֵי שְׁפֹט הַשֹּׁפְטִים time-notice that regularly launches a fresh narrative frame; the unit narrates one continuous causal chain (famine forces emigration, husband dies, sons marry and then also die) without a scene-relocation or new speaker interrupting the narrator's voice. Verse 2's own disjunctive, verbless naming clause (וְשֵׁ֣ם הָאִ֣ישׁ אֱֽלִימֶ֡לֶךְ) does not register as an independent seam of the kind found at 2:1 or 4:7: it names participants already inventoried in v1's household roster (ה֥וּא וְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ וּשְׁנֵ֥י בָנָֽיו), functioning as an appositive supplying detail within this single already-bounded exposition unit rather than introducing a participant genuinely new to the story ahead of a scene of his own — the test that lets 2:1 earn its own, weaker seam in decision 005 — and it carries none of the temporal deictic that places 4:7's aside outside story-time altogether in decision 015. It closes on וַתִּשָּׁאֵר הָאִשָּׁה מִשְּׁנֵי יְלָדֶיהָ וּמֵאִישָׁהּ, a bereavement formula that mirrors and inverts the household inventory given in v1 — the same husband/wife/two-sons triad now stripped to the widow alone, closing the exposition's arithmetic. The next verse pivots on a new subject-led movement verb (וַתָּקָם הִיא וְכַלֹּתֶיהָ), introducing the daughters-in-law as active participants for the first time and initiating the return journey the exposition never narrates.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through v7 (to include the notice that Naomi heard the famine had ended and set out) was considered, since v6's פָקַ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת עַמּ֔וֹ לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם לָֽחֶם answers the רָעָב of v1 and could be read as the exposition's true resolution. Rejected because vv.6-7 introduce a new grammatical subject-cluster (Naomi with 'her daughters-in-law,' a phrase absent from vv.1-5) and a new narrative goal (the road back to Judah) that belongs with the dialogue it sets up rather than with the family's death-notices.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the new movement verb noted above (וַתָּקָם...וַתָּשָׁב) and stays grammatically plural-addressed throughout: Naomi's two speeches in this span (v8's לֵ֣כְנָה שֹּׁ֔בְנָה and v11-12's שֹׁ֤בְנָה בְנֹתַי / לֵ֔כְןָ) both use feminine-plural imperatives directed at BOTH daughters-in-law together, and the weeping that answers each speech is explicitly doubled — v14's וַתִּשֶּׂ֣נָה קוֹלָ֔ן וַתִּבְכֶּ֖ינָה ע֑וֹד uses עוֹד to hook back to the identical phrase in v9, marking the two weeping episodes as one resumed emotional beat rather than two separate scenes. Both v8 and v11 open with the same named-speaker formula, וַתֹּ֤אמֶר נָעֳמִי֙, which on its face looks like it could reset the unit twice; it does not, because a repeated named-speaker formula functions as a turn marker rather than a scene-reset throughout this dialogue-dense book — the clearest proof is Ruth 2:20 (decision 010), which carries the identical formula twice inside one unbroken exchange with no addressee change. Applying that same principle here, neither v8 nor v11 carries the second signal (relocation, addressee change, elapsed time) that a genuine seam requires, so the real binding device remains the עוֹד-Wiederaufnahme at v14, not the repeated speech-tags. The span ends the moment the audience narrows: v14b singles out Orpah's kiss and departure against וְר֖וּת דָּ֥בְקָה בָּֽהּ ('but Ruth clung to her'), and every verb of address from v15 on shifts to feminine-singular forms aimed at Ruth alone.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating vv.8-10, 11-13, and 14 as three separate decisions (one per Naomi speech-turn) was considered, since each speech is introduced by an explicit-subject וַתֹּאמֶר נָעֳמִי. Rejected because a repeated named-speaker formula is a turn marker in this book, not a unit-opener by itself — reading every such formula as a reset would fragment this and other dialogues into unwarranted single-turn pieces, exactly the mistake decision 010 avoids when it declines to cut Ruth 2:20's doubled וַתֹּאמֶר נָעֳמִי formula into two units — and because the doubled weeping refrain (עוֹד at v14 recalling v9) functions as the actual resumptive device binding the two speech-rounds into a single scene, with no relocation, new addressee, or elapsed time separating the speeches beyond the refusal-and-repeat rhythm of one ongoing roadside appeal.

boundary_rationale: This span opens with the address narrowing to Ruth alone (שׁ֖וּבִי, a feminine-singular imperative, against the plural imperatives of the preceding unit), Naomi's final, brief appeal pointing to Orpah's example. Ruth's reply (וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רוּת, an explicit-subject speech-formula naming her for the first time as the sole respondent) is the celebrated parallelistic pledge of vv.16-17, and the unit is closed off by the narrator's summary verdict in v18: וַתֵּ֕רֶא כִּֽי מִתְאַמֶּ֥צֶת הִ֖יא לָלֶ֣כֶת אִתָּ֑הּ וַתֶּחְדַּ֖ל לְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶֽיהָ ('she stopped speaking to her') — a discourse-ending tag with no further quoted words, distinct in kind from the resumed-journey narration that opens the next span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating vv.16-17 (the oath itself) as a standalone decision was considered, given its distinct poetic cadence and its frequent treatment as a self-contained set-piece in commentary. Rejected because it carries no independent scene-marker of its own — no time notice, no relocation, no new addressee — and is introduced by the same ordinary narrative speech-frame used throughout this conversation; its poetic register is a function of content and rhetorical intensity, not of a textual seam, so lifting it out would sever it from the appeal (v15) it directly answers and the narrator's verdict (v18) it provokes.

boundary_rationale: The span begins with a fresh dual-subject movement verb, וַתֵּלַ֣כְנָה שְׁתֵּיהֶ֔ם ('the two of them went'), resuming the journey after the roadside dialogue closed and carrying it to its destination; the arrival is stated twice in close succession (עַד בֹּאָנָה בֵּית לָחֶם / כְּבֹאָנָה בֵּית לֶחֶם), a doubling that frames the 'is this Naomi?' commotion and the Mara speech it triggers. The span closes with v22's own restatement of the same arrival-notice — וְהֵ֗מָּה בָּ֚אוּ בֵּ֣ית לֶ֔חֶם — a resumptive echo of v19 that folds the embedded Mara dialogue inside a repeated-arrival frame, and appends the harvest timestamp the next chapter's field scene depends on.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting the unit at v19/20 (separating the townswomen's arrival-notice from the Mara speech proper) was considered, since v20 opens with a fresh וַתֹּאמֶר. Rejected because the 'is this Naomi?' question (v19b) has no self-contained content apart from setting up Naomi's answer, and because the resumptive arrival-notice at v22 only makes sense as the closing counterpart to v19's arrival-notice — separating them would strand the frame's second half from its first.

boundary_rationale: This single verse is built as a disjunctive, verbless circumstantial clause — וּֽלְנָעֳמִ֞י מוֹדַ֣ע לְאִישָׁ֗הּ ('and-to-Naomi [there was] a kinsman') fronts the prepositional phrase ahead of any finite verb, taking the narration off the wayyiqtol storyline to supply background the reader needs before the action resumes. The following verse returns to ordinary narrative sequence with an explicit-subject wayyiqtol, וַתֹּאמֶר֩ ר֨וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֜ה, restarting the plot. Disjunctive verbless syntax by itself is necessary but not sufficient to register its own seam in this book: the differentiating test is whether the clause introduces a participant genuinely new to the story ahead of that participant's own scene, and whether it further carries a temporal deictic placing the narrator outside story-time. Ruth 1:2 (וְשֵׁ֣ם הָאִ֣ישׁ אֱֽלִימֶ֡לֶךְ), the same construction type, fails the first test — it merely names participants already inventoried in 1:1's household roster and is rightly absorbed into decision 001 with no separate seam. Ruth 4:7 (וְזֹאת֩ לְפָנִ֨ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל) passes both tests, since לְפָנִים adds a signal this verse lacks, which is why 4:7 is priced at high in decision 015 while this verse is not. This verse passes only the first test: Boaz is wholly new to the story and his introduction runs well ahead of his actual entrance at 2:4, earning a real but comparatively modest seam. The seam is genuine but the span itself is a single informational clause satisfying only one of the two tests, so confidence is priced down accordingly.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this verse into vv.2-3 as the opening of one 'setup' unit was considered, since nothing happens narratively in v1 by itself. Rejected because the verse passes the new-participant test stated above, sharing its verbless, no-finite-verb shape with 4:7's aside (וְזֹאת֩ לְפָנִ֨ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל) — though 4:1's וּבֹ֨עַז עָלָ֣ה הַשַּׁעַר֮ is a related but distinct subject-fronted qatal clause with a finite verb, not a true syntactic parallel to this verse or to 4:7 — and because its content, establishing Boaz's status and lineage before Ruth 'happens' into his field, sets up dramatic irony that depends on being logically prior to, not fused with, Ruth's own initiative in v2.

boundary_rationale: The span opens with Ruth's own initiative, an explicit-subject speech-formula requesting permission to glean, and Naomi's terse consent (לְכִ֥י בִתִּֽי), then narrates her going out and the 'chance' that lands her in Boaz's field — closing on the loaded notice וַיִּ֣קֶר מִקְרֶ֔הָ חֶלְקַ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ לְבֹ֔עַז, naming the very field the reader was primed for in v1. The next verse opens with וְהִנֵּה בֹ֗עַז בָּ֚א, a הִנֵּה-marked entrance that shifts the narrative's viewpoint to track Boaz's arrival on scene, a distinct visual/participant cue absent from this span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this span forward into vv.4-7 (treating 'Ruth goes to the field' through 'Boaz identifies her' as one continuous field-arrival unit) was considered. Rejected because v3's 'chance' notice is a self-contained narratorial punchline that pays off v1's introduction of Boaz, and the הִנֵּה of v4 marks a genuine viewpoint shift onto a new participant entering the scene, which is a stronger seam than anything internal to vv.2-3.

boundary_rationale: Both edges of this span are independently marked. It opens on the הִנֵּה-fronted entrance already noted, introducing Boaz onto the scene and his greeting-exchange with the reapers (יְהוָ֣ה עִמָּכֶ֑ם / יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ יְהוָֽה), then moves to his question about Ruth's identity addressed to his servant and the servant's answering report. It closes exactly where the addressee changes: v8 opens וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶל ר֜וּת, the first time in the chapter Boaz speaks directly TO Ruth rather than ABOUT her in the third person to an intermediary — a clean, checkable shift in who is being addressed.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v4 (the reaper-greeting) from vv.5-7 (the servant-inquiry) was considered, since they are formally distinct exchanges with different interlocutors. Rejected because both exchanges share the same participants on scene, the same location, and no time elapses between them — the greeting establishes Boaz's character immediately before the inquiry that turns his attention toward Ruth, and dividing a four-verse span into two two-verse fragments over an internal addressee change (reapers vs. servant) would be finer-grained than the addressee change that closes the whole span (about Ruth vs. to Ruth).

boundary_rationale: This span is anchored by the recurring favor-word (חן) figure, but the figure is a three-member chain beginning at 2:2 (אֶמְצָא חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֑יו, Ruth's request to Naomi, outside this span and inside decision 006) and continuing within this span at 2:10 (מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙, Ruth's question to Boaz) and 2:13 (אֶמְצָא חֵ֨ן בְּעֵינֶ֤יךָ אֲדֹנִי֙, her closing line to him) — a span-internal echo running 2:10-to-2:13, starting two verses inside the opening edge, not a bracket enclosing the whole 2:8-13 unit. The opening edge of this span is independently carried by Boaz's direct address to Ruth noted in decision 007 (וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶל ר֜וּת). The closing edge is softer than a bracket-reading implies: 2:14's לְעֵ֣ת הָאֹ֗כֶל is post-verbal (וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לָ֨ה בֹ֜עַז לְעֵ֣ת הָאֹ֗כֶל) rather than clause-initial, and the speaker-addressee pair (Boaz to Ruth) is unchanged from v13. The stronger, span-internal candidate for a closing signal sits one verse later, at 2:15's וַיְצַו֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶת נְעָרָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר, which pairs a named subject with a genuinely new addressee (the young men, not Ruth) — the same signal pair decision 007 treats as seam-grade at 2:7/2:8. The span itself still stands, opened cleanly at 2:8 and closed reasonably at the mealtime pivot of 2:14, but only one edge (the opening) carries full seam-grade signal strength; the closing edge rests on a weaker, non-clause-initial temporal marker rather than on the חן figure, which is internal to the span rather than bracketing it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating Boaz's instructions (vv.8-9) from the favor-exchange proper (vv.10-13) was considered, since v8-9 is imperative/instructional in mood while v10-13 is question-and-blessing. Rejected because Ruth's question in v10 is a direct response to the instructions just given, and the 2:10-to-2:13 חן echo — not a full bracket, since its first member sits at 2:2 — still binds v10 to v13 as one exchange internal to this span. A second alternative, ending the span at 2:13 rather than 2:14, was also weighed against extending it through 2:15, since 2:15's named-subject-plus-new-addressee pairing (וַיְצַו֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶת נְעָרָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר) is formally a stronger signal than 2:14's post-verbal mealtime notice. Rejected in favor of the 2:13/14 cut because 2:14 already introduces a genuinely fresh topic (provision/food) absent from the favor-exchange, even though its own marking is comparatively soft — a softness now reflected in the span's confidence rather than papered over by an inclusio claim the text does not fully support.

boundary_rationale: The span opens on a fresh temporal marker, לְעֵ֣ת הָאֹ֗כֶל ('at mealtime'), pivoting the scene from the favor-dialogue to provision — the shared meal, then Boaz's supplementary instructions to the young men to deliberately leave extra grain for her. It closes on a quantified summary, וַיְהִ֖י כְּאֵיפָ֥ה שְׂעֹרִֽים ('it was about an ephah of barley'), a tally that answers the implicit question of a gleaning narrative before v18 pivots to a new movement verb and location (וַתִּשָּׂא֙ וַתָּב֣וֹא הָעִ֔יר, 'she took it up and went into the city').
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating vv.15-16 (Boaz's renewed instructions to the young men) as a separate decision from v14 (the meal) was considered, since they address different listeners (Ruth vs. the reapers). Rejected because both beats serve the same narrative function — Boaz quietly ensuring Ruth's provision exceeds what her own labor would secure — and neither carries an independent time, place, or participant marker strong enough to divide them; the ephah-tally at v17 is the first real closural device after v14, and it closes both beats together.

boundary_rationale: The span begins with Ruth's return to the city and to Naomi (a location/participant shift from the field), moves through Naomi's questioning, the naming of Boaz, and Naomi's recognition of him as a גֹּאֵל ('redeemer') — the first appearance in the book of the legal term that will drive the rest of the plot — and closes on a chapter-length time-summary, עַד כְּל֥וֹת קְצִ֣יר הַשְּׂעֹרִ֖ים וּקְצִ֣יר הַֽחִטִּ֑ים ('until the end of barley harvest and wheat harvest'), which compresses the remainder of the season before ch.3 opens on Naomi's new initiative. The v20 recognition is anchored inside this span rather than split off, by a principle this book applies consistently: a named-speaker formula functions here as a turn marker within a running exchange, not as a scene-reset in its own right. Verse 20 itself supplies the clearest proof — it carries the identical formula וַתֹּאמֶר נָעֳמִי twice (וַתֹּ֨אמֶר נָעֳמִ֜י לְכַלָּתָ֗הּ ... וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ נָעֳמִ֗י) inside one uninterrupted conversation with no addressee change, the same pattern this book uses at 1:8 and 1:11 within a single appeal-and-refusal scene (decision 002). Reading every repeated speech-tag as an opener would fragment this dialogue into unwarranted two-verse pieces; the actual seams bounding this span are the location shift at v18 and the season-summary at v23.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off v20 (Naomi's גֹּאֵל recognition) as its own decision was considered, given its outsized thematic weight for the plot. Rejected because it is syntactically just the continuation of the same question-and-answer report Ruth and Naomi are having — no new speech-frame introduces a scene break, the repeated וַתֹּאמֶר נָעֳמִי formula within v20 itself functions as a turn marker rather than a reset (the same principle applied at 1:8/1:11 in decision 002), and the conversation carries on without interruption through v22 — so isolating a single thematically important clause from its surrounding dialogue would privilege content-importance over an actual textual seam, which the binding rules for this book do not permit.

boundary_rationale: This span opens the chapter with Naomi's explicit-subject speech-formula, וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ נָעֳמִ֣י חֲמוֹתָ֑הּ, and her proposal to seek 'rest' (מָנ֖וֹחַ) for Ruth — a term that echoes, as a cognate nominal form of the same root נוח rather than the identical word, Naomi's own מְנוּחָ֔ה-wish for her daughters-in-law in 1:9, marking this as the start of a new initiative rather than a continuation of the previous chapter's harvest-summary. The unit is entirely instructional in content (wash, anoint, dress, go down, wait, note, uncover, lie down) and closes the moment Ruth gives her formulaic assent, כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר תֹּאמְרִ֥י אֵלַ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶֽׂה ('all that you say, I will do'), before the narration shifts to executed action.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through v6 (to include 'she went down and did as her mother-in-law commanded') was considered, since v6 could read as simply completing Naomi's sentence. Rejected because v6 is a narrator's compressed EXECUTION notice, using indirect summary (כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוַּ֖תָּה חֲמוֹתָֽהּ) rather than repeating the instructions verbatim, which is the book's regular device for marking the transition from planning-speech to enacted narrative — the true parallel is 2:2's request (אֵֽלְכָה נָּ֤א הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וַאֲלַקֳטָּ֣ה בַשִׁבֳּלִ֔ים) answered by 2:3's own compressed summary (וַתֵּ֤לֶךְ וַתָּבוֹא֙ וַתְּלַקֵּ֣ט בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה), not the instruction/fulfillment pattern later in this same chapter at 3:13/3:14. That later pair is in fact the opposite pattern — a near-verbatim repetition (שִׁכְבִ֖י עַד הַבֹּֽקֶר answered by וַתִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מַרְגְּלוֹתָיוֹ֙ עַד הַבֹּ֔קֶר) that this record's own decision 012 correctly treats as a continuity-binding echo rather than a compression device, and so is a counterexample to, not a parallel for, the compressed-summary claim made here.

boundary_rationale: This span covers one unbroken stretch of time and place — the threshing floor from nightfall to just before dawn — opened by the compressed execution notice discussed above and closed only when Boaz physically leaves the scene, וַיָּבֹ֖א הָעִֽיר ('he went into the city,' v15b), a location-change verb ending the encounter. Internally the span contains a temporal marker, עַד הַבֹּקֶר ('until morning'), used both in Boaz's instruction at v13 and in the narration of its fulfillment at v14 — a verbal echo this campaign's precedent treats as evidence of continuity binding the material together, not as grounds for a further split between the midnight dialogue and the pre-dawn departure. The span's strongest internal rival, the seam at 3:7/3:8, is engaged and refused below rather than left untested.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Dividing this span at 3:7/3:8 was considered and is the genuinely strongest rival, not the 13/14 division. Verse 8 stacks two device types this record treats as seam-grade elsewhere into a single verse: a fronted temporal clause, וַיְהִי֙ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַלַּ֔יְלָה ('and it happened at midnight'), the only construction of its kind in the book apart from 1:1 and the arrival-frame inside 1:19, immediately followed by a presentative clause, וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִשָּׁ֔ה שֹׁכֶ֖בֶת מַרְגְּלֹתָֽיו ('and behold, a woman lying at his feet'), the same הִנֵּה-device treated as seam-grade at 2:4 (decision 007) and 4:1 (decision 014). Refused on the following ground: the presentative at 3:8 reports Boaz's startled perception of a person already on stage — Ruth arrived and lay down at his feet in 3:7 (וַתָּבֹ֣א בַלָּ֔ט וַתְּגַ֥ל מַרְגְּלֹתָ֖יו וַתִּשְׁכָּֽב), one verse earlier within this same span — whereas the הִנֵּה-presentatives at 2:4 and 4:1 walk a genuinely fresh participant onto an empty stage from outside it. The midnight notice similarly times a moment inside an already-running encounter rather than opening a new frame. A secondary division at 3:13/3:14 (separating the midnight dialogue from the dawn rising and the gift of barley) was also weighed, precisely because of the 'until morning' repetition and the shift from dialogue to narration it introduces, and is rejected on the same continuity ground: the repetition is a resumptive device signaling fulfillment of an instruction just given, not a scene break, so treating either internal repetition as a split point would mistake a continuity or perception marker for a boundary marker.

boundary_rationale: The span opens with a location/participant shift back to Naomi (וַתָּבוֹא֙ אֶל חֲמוֹתָ֔הּ), whose opening question, מִ֣י אַ֣תְּ בִּתִּ֑י ('who are you, my daughter'), deliberately echoes Boaz's own מִי אָ֑תּ at the midnight encounter (v9), framing this closing report as a structural counterpart to the night scene it recounts. It closes the chapter on Naomi's forward-looking counsel, כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִשְׁקֹט֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ כִּֽי אִם כִּלָּ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַיּֽוֹם ('the man will not rest until he has settled this today'), a statement whose fulfillment is precisely what ch.4 opens by narrating.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this span backward into the threshing-floor unit (treating the whole of 3:6-18 as one report-inclusive scene) was considered, since Ruth's report recounts events already narrated to the reader. Rejected because a genuine location and participant shift occurs at v16 — the scene physically returns to Naomi's household — and because Naomi's closing counsel is addressed to the reader's anticipation of ch.4 rather than to anything within the threshing-floor encounter itself, making it a distinct unit rather than a coda glued onto the night scene.

boundary_rationale: The chapter opens with a subject-fronted clause, וּבֹ֨עַז עָלָ֣ה הַשַּׁעַר֮ ('and Boaz went up to the gate'), the verb placed after its subject rather than in the ordinary wayyiqtol-initial slot — a scene-launching construction paired with a wholly new location (the town gate) and, moments later, another הִנֵּה-marked entrance for the near-kinsman, echoing the device used to introduce Boaz himself in 2:4. The span covers the entire legal setup and land-redemption negotiation, closing on the kinsman's cession, גְּאַל לְךָ֤ אַתָּה֙ אֶת גְּאֻלָּתִ֔י ('redeem for yourself my right of redemption'), immediately before the narrator interrupts the scene with an explanatory aside.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the convening of witnesses (vv.1-2) from the negotiation proper (vv.3-6) was considered, since the content shifts from assembling participants to conducting business. Rejected because no textual marker separates them — the same wayyiqtol chain runs through both without a change of location, speaker set, or time, and the assembling of the ten elders in v2 is simply the necessary precondition the negotiation of vv.3-6 requires; dividing on topic alone, absent a text signal, would be exactly the kind of over-splitting this book's binding rules warn against.

web:Ruth.4.6 Take my right of redemption for yourself; for I can't redeem it.

boundary_rationale: This single verse is marked off by the same disjunctive syntax used at 2:1, opening with a fronted demonstrative rather than a wayyiqtol, וְזֹאת֩ לְפָנִ֨ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל ('now this was formerly the custom in Israel'), and its temporal deictic לְפָנִים ('in former times') explicitly places the narrator's own vantage point AFTER and outside the story-time being narrated — the clearest signal in the book of the narrator addressing the reader directly rather than reporting character speech or action. Bare disjunctive, verbless syntax alone is not sufficient to earn its own seam in this book: compare 1:2 in decision 001, absorbed with no separate seam because it only names participants already inventoried in v1's roster. What earns a seam is passing at least one of two further tests — introducing a participant genuinely new to the story ahead of that participant's own scene (which is what earns 2:1 its own, weaker seam in decision 005), or carrying a temporal deictic of this kind. This verse passes the second test, independently of introducing any new participant at all, which is why it is priced three steps above 2:1 rather than merely one. The very next verse resumes ordinary narrative sequence with an explicit-subject wayyiqtol, וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַגֹּאֵ֛ל, and the kinsman enacts, in real time, the sandal-custom the aside just explained.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this verse into v8 (treating the explanation and its enactment as one 'sandal custom' unit) was considered, since v8 is effectively the aside's own illustration. Rejected because the disjunctive-clause marker is a discourse-level signal, not a content-level one — the same test applied at 2:1 — and the aside is grammatically and temporally addressed to the reader across the gap between narrated events and the narrator's present, which is a genuinely different mode of speech from the wayyiqtol-narrated enactment that follows it.

boundary_rationale: The span resumes with the kinsman's sandal removal (enacting the just-explained custom) and moves directly into Boaz's own formal proclamation. That proclamation is framed by the witness formula עֵדִים אַתֶּם הַיּוֹם as a true inclusio rather than a matched pair of end-tags: in 4:9 the formula stands speech-initial, at the sixth through eighth words of Boaz's declaration — וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז לַזְּקֵנִ֜ים וְכָל הָעָ֗ם עֵדִ֤ים אַתֶּם֙ הַיּ֔וֹם — immediately after he addresses the elders and all the people and directly before the causal כִּי that introduces the acquisition clause (כִּ֤י קָנִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֶֽאֱלִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְכִלְי֖וֹן וּמַחְל֑וֹן מִיַּ֖ד נָעֳמִֽי) — while in 4:10 the identical formula, עֵדִ֥ים אַתֶּ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם, stands speech-final, closing the verse and the whole declaration. The frame therefore opens at the head of v9 and closes at the tail of v10, bracketing both the land-purchase clause and the levirate-wife clause as one continuous legal statement — a genuine opening-and-closing inclusio, which is stronger evidence for treating the proclamation as a single unit than a pair of repeated end-tags would have been. It closes the instant a different, plural subject takes over the speaking role: v11 opens וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ כָּל הָעָ֧ם אֲשֶׁר בַּשַּׁ֛עַר וְהַזְּקֵנִ֖ים, the assembled crowd's own voice replacing Boaz's.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the sandal-transfer narrative (v8) from Boaz's proclamation (vv.9-10) was considered, since one is narrated action and the other is direct speech. Rejected because the sandal transfer is the physical enactment that Boaz's own opening words in v9 immediately refer back to (קָנִיתִי, 'I have bought/acquired,' presupposes the just-completed exchange of the sandal), so the two halves of this span depend on each other for their sense and share the same participants and setting without a break.

literature_type_guess: narrative with embedded communal blessing formula
boundary_rationale: This short span is the assembly's antiphonal answer to Boaz's proclamation, opened by the explicit-subject reset just noted (the people and elders replacing Boaz as speaker) and linked to what precedes by the catchword עֵדִים ('witnesses') repeated from the close of v10 into the crowd's own first word — a hinge marking both continuity of topic and change of speaker. It closes on the Perez/Tamar blessing, itself a forward-pointing detail anticipating the toledot genealogy at the chapter's end, before v13's wayyiqtol narrates the blessing's fulfillment.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this span with vv.8-10 into one undivided 'gate ceremony' unit was considered, since the catchword linkage argues for close continuity rather than sharp division. Rejected, though with some hesitation reflected in the confidence rating, because the explicit change of speaking subject (from Boaz individually to the assembled people and elders collectively) is a real, checkable marker distinguishing proclamation from communal ratification, even though the two are thematically and lexically bound together by the shared witness-language.

literature_type_guess: narrative with embedded communal speech (birth and naming scene)
boundary_rationale: The span opens on a wayyiqtol fulfillment — וַיִּקַּ֨ח בֹּ֤עַז אֶת רוּת֙ וַתְּהִי ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה ('so Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife') — narrating, as accomplished fact, exactly what the assembly's jussive blessing in v12 had only wished for, a wish-then-fulfillment shift that marks a real seam. Within the span the neighbor-women speak twice (a blessing at vv.14-15 and a naming-formula at v17) around Naomi's own adoptive gesture (v16), but no relocation or elapsed time separates any of these beats, so they are kept together as one birth-and-naming scene. The span closes on the genealogical tag ה֥וּא אֲבִי יִשַׁ֖י אֲבִ֥י דָוִֽד ('he is the father of Jesse, the father of David'), immediately before the formal תּוֹלְדוֹת heading of v18 shifts the text into a different genre altogether.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the neighbor-women's two speeches (vv.14-15 and v17) as distinct decisions, with Naomi's nursing gesture (v16) forming a third, was considered, since each beat has its own explicit-subject introduction. Rejected because none of the three beats is marked off by any scene-level signal (no new location, no new time, no new participant set — the same women, Naomi, and the child remain constant throughout), and fragmenting a five-beat scene at every internal speech-turn would produce single-verse decisions with no independent textual warrant, unlike the aside at 4:7 or the character-introduction at 2:1, both of which carry a genuine disjunctive-clause marker that this material lacks.

web:Ruth.4.17 He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

boundary_rationale: This span opens with an unmistakable formal genre-marker, the תולדות-heading וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ תּוֹלְד֣וֹת פָּ֔רֶץ ('now these are the generations of Perez'), the same fixed formula used elsewhere in the canon to open a genealogical section — at Genesis 2:4, 25:19, and 37:2, for instance, the identical heading opens a section that goes on to narrate rather than merely list, so the formula itself marks a section boundary and does not by itself guarantee register-only content. What makes this span function as a register is internal to Ruth's own text: it proceeds as a uniform ten-member הוֹלִיד ('became the father of') chain with no narrative or dialogue content at all, closing the book on the name דָּוִֽד ('David') toward which the whole chain has been building. The book's single parashah mark (a pe, per the two-witness freeze file, with both OSHB and UXLC agreeing) falls after 4:17 — exactly at the seam between the narrative ending and this genealogical register — and is cited here as weak corroboration only, consistent with this book's near-total marker silence, never as a driver of the decision itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Subdividing the genealogy internally (for instance, separating the heading v18 from the chain, or breaking the ten links into smaller groups) was considered. Rejected under this book's list/register-function principle: a formulaic genealogical chain with no internal variation in form functions as a single unit by genre convention, and slicing it verse-by-verse would treat each 'begat' clause as if it carried independent narrative weight, which it does not — the register's function is cumulative and only complete at David's name.
